sara_support: Hey team — customer reported invoice total != ledger export after currency conversion. They see a 0.03 EUR gap on invoice 2026-03-02. Dashboard usage matches our API logs though. Can billing take a look? :thinking:

jamal_billing: Thanks Sara. Can you paste the invoice id and the CSV export they downloaded? Also what currency was the account set to?

sara_support: Invoice ID INV-2026-00321, account currency EUR. Attached CSV snippet they sent: 
```
line_item,usage,unit_price,total
req-1,1234 tokens,0.0004 EUR,0.4936
req-2,450 tokens,0.0004 EUR,0.1800
req-3,987 tokens,0.0004 EUR,0.3948
subtotal,, ,1.0684
tax 20%,, ,0.2137
total,, ,1.2821
```
They say our dashboard shows subtotal 1.0683 and invoice 1.2820. So dashboard vs invoice both off by -0.01 or -0.03 depending on rounding.

jamal_billing: Hmm. Looks like per-line rounding vs per-request aggregation. Our invoice generator currently rounds each line item to 4 decimal places then sums, then applies tax and rounds to 4. The dashboard rolls up raw microcent-level values and rounds only at display to 2 decimals. That can create small deltas.

ana_engineer: tagging in Ana from infra — Ana, we pushed a change last quarter that changed tokenization accounting to count tokens at the model decode step vs request header estimate. Could this cause the mismatch? It should affect counts not tiny cents, but worth checking. @ana_engineer any known rounding policy changes in billing pipeline?

ana_engineer: hey — no billing policy change from infra side. We did change how tokens are counted (more accurate), but that affects token totals, not rounding. However I recall the invoice generator does currency conversion before tax and sometimes applies per-line currency rounding to 2 decimals early if invoice currency != billing denom. Could be the convert-then-round bug.

jamal_billing: That could be it. Customer was billed in EUR but our internal usage ledger is in USD. Sequence: compute USD cost per request -> convert to EUR (multiply by rate) -> round to 2dp per-line -> sum -> apply VAT -> final round. Dashboard shows converted total after summing then rounding at display. When rates produce fractional cents, different order gives 0.01-0.03 diffs.

sara_support: Customer is asking for a clear explanation and a corrected invoice if we were wrong. They provided a small repro: export ledger in USD then run our conversion script with the rate used on invoice day. I ran it quickly and got 0.03EUR difference, matches invoice.

ana_engineer: Can you paste the repro steps? I can run locally.

sara_support: Sure — they provided this command: 
```
# ledger.csv has usage_usd per-request
python tools/convert_currency.py --input ledger.csv --from USD --to EUR --rate 0.91425 --round-per-line
```
They also tried `--round-after-sum` and got the dashboard number.

ana_engineer: Ok I can reproduce. There's an earlier patch where we added `--round-per-line` for legal reasons in some regions, but that should have been behind a feature flag per-customer. Looks like a flag misconfiguration: this account has the flag enabled inadvertently.

jamal_billing: If flagged per-customer we need to correct behavior: either reissue invoice with consistent rounding policy or provide adjustment line. For EU customers VAT rules expect invoice arithmetic to be explicit. We should consult finance. @mike_prod can you loop in finance?

mike_prod: looping in finance now. Meanwhile, to help the customer: offer a one-time credit of 0.03 EUR if they want immediate compensation, and escalate for invoice reissue if required. Also include explanation about conversion and rounding.

sara_support: Customer asked if token counting affects totals — they also noticed ~2 token discrepancy on a few requests. Ana, are tokenization differences safe to ignore?

ana_engineer: 2-token diffs per-request could be due to model tokenizer updates. For large customers we store both estimated_token_count and final_token_count; invoices use final. If they have cached dashboard metrics derived from estimates, that would explain small token deltas. I'll confirm which field the dashboard pulls.

jamal_billing: Action items: 1) Confirm feature flag mismatch caused per-line rounding (ana) 2) If yes, run backfill to compute corrected invoice totals with round-after-sum and decide reissue (billing) 3) Offer customer credit and explanation (sara + mike) 4) Add an integration test to prevent this config drift (ana + eng infra)

billing-bot: [automated] Ticket TKT-9421 created: "INV NUMBR: INV-2026-00321 - rounding discrepancy investigation" assigned to jamal_billing.

sara_support: Customer replied: "Credit would be fine, please also re-run invoice math and confirm in writing. We'd like to avoid discrepancies going forward." I'll send the credit offer and hold reissue until finance confirms.

ana_engineer: Found the flag in customer profile: `eu_invoice_rounding_policy: per_line` set by migration script for EU batch. That was supposed to be set only for legacy accounts. I'll patch migration and schedule a roll-forward to set `per_line` only for legacy_legacy.

jamal_billing: Great. For transparency, let's produce a short note explaining the difference: include pseudo-math showing convert->round per-line vs sum->convert then round. Sara, draft that for customer.

sara_support: Draft ready: "We found that during invoice generation your account was subject to a per-line currency rounding policy. This causes the invoice total to differ from the dashboard by a few cents when conversion rates produce fractional cents. We can issue a corrected invoice using a sum-then-round arithmetic, or apply a one-time adjustment credit. We are fixing the config to prevent recurrence." Will send after finance confirms.

mike_prod: Finance signed off: reissue allowed for small deltas under 0.10 EUR. Proceed with invoice reissue plus note. Mike approves 0.03 EUR credit if customer prefers credit instead.

jamal_billing: I'll run the reissue script and attach the corrected invoice, and keep original for audit. Also adding unit test for conversion path. ETA 24h.

sara_support: Thanks all. I'll update the customer and close once they've accepted credit or we reissue. :thumbsup:

billing-bot: [automated] Ticket TKT-9421 status updated to "in_progress" assigned to jamal_billing.

sara_support: (after reissue) Reissue done — new invoice INV-2026-00321-R1 total 1.2820 EUR, credit line 0.03 EUR added to account. Customer accepted and closed. :white_check_mark:
